source.snippet: The third week of October 2026 was a rough one for anyone who runs software on the internet. Two [incidents described]. Hours, Not Weeks: How AI Rewrote the Clock of Software Security — small teams are falling behind. Score 30, 36 comments, tagged: security, ai, startup, discuss.

problem_statement: Small engineering teams cannot keep pace with AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploit development, leaving their production software exposed for days or weeks while attackers now operate on a timescale of hours.
target_segment: CTOs and lead engineers at startups and SMBs (2–50 person eng teams) running internet-facing software without a dedicated security function
notes: Article scored 30 with 36 comments on dev.to — meaningful engagement signal for a practitioner audience. The pain is structural (speed asymmetry between attackers and defenders) and well-documented in paid markets: SMB security tooling is a large category (Snyk, Wiz, Semgrep all have paying customers at this segment). Buyer signal: startups do pay for security tooling, especially post-incident or under compliance pressure. Body text truncated but framing implies concrete recent incidents. Signal strength 3: editorial piece with engagement, known paid category, but no direct 'I'd pay for X' quote visible in snippet.
